Winston Fani Africas First Blind Tour Guide

By: Diana Lucas | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Meet Nqabohlanga Winston Fani – Africa’s first Blind Tour Guide

His tours have been described as unique, evocative, fascinating and expect the unexpected. Winston Fani is blind and in his words:

For people who are blind they don’t see with the naked eye they see with the eyes of the heart but in order for the eyes of the heart to kick in you have to give people a picture.

A two hour walking tour through the heart of Salt River, Cape Town, is Winstons flagship project. A unique expedition for sighted and the visually impaired, taking in giant artwork and intimate local art studios where sculptured and diverse artistic endeavours come to life. A lot of the artworks now have QR codes, which lead you to audio clips with Winston’s voice giving the detail. Despite having never seen the artwork, he describes the murals and unpacks the work with those on tours with him.


Further information:
It’s easy to forget Winston is a blind guide but an enormous amount of preparation and research goes into his tours. Counting steps between stops, talking to the artists, creating a whole new language in describing the attractions through his blind eyes.

Winston was born partially sighted and at age 11 lost his sight altogether. In 2020 – with the onset of COVID- he was retrenched from his job at a call centre. Work was hard to find, Winston and his wife Busisiwe – also blind- moved from Parklands to Umfoleni.

Why this vocation? An unrealistic and un likely career choice given the circumstances

His beginnings of guiding had an unlikely start . Tanya Robertze, who raised Gladys – Busisiwe’s guide dog – wanted to visit. Winston gave her directions to his new home over the phone – without ever having seen the route. Tanya was amazed saying if you can navigate yourself in this busy area what’s stopping you working as a tour guide. Winston’s passion for history and education, his ability to connect with people, great assets for tour guiding.

Tanya started a Back-a-Buddy fund, Winston went on radio where CEO of Cape Tourism, Enver Duminy heard him and paid for the costs of Winston’s training

Winston doesn’t feel he has any different challenges from sighted people, he says the key to overcoming challenges is don’t put barriers in front of yourself but studying to become a tour guide presented challenges: He had to navigate public transport to Century City and walk more than a kilometre to his classes. There were also assignments and visiting areas to learn about their history.

In 2023 he completed his guiding course and he has been guiding for around a year

You’re performing in front of people you’re representing the whole country every time you do it because this is important every time tourists come have a fantastic experience you are doing something on a very powerful level?

Script:


UPSOUND WINSTON:
Ladies and Gentlemen I want us to stand here…look at the mural that is titled man with dreadlocks. The artist who did this mural his name is May, he's from France. He was born in 1990.
V/O
Winston Fani is a tour guide working in Cape Town
UPS Winston:
His beard is made of bushes, he looks like a Rasta
V/O
He’s taking us on a walk through the suburb of Salt River for a unique perspective on the local street art.
UPS Winston:
Every art work on this tour there is a theme behind it
UPS Winston:
My name is Winston Fani, I am the first blind tour guide in Africa, possibly in the world.
V/O **
The story of how Winston went from a call-centre agent to a much-loved tour guide, was – some might say – written in the stars…
The beginning of Winston’s career change had an unlikely start. Meet Gladys who is Winston’s wife Busisiwe’s Guide dog.
V/O ***
Like Winston Busisiwe is also blind. Gladys was raised by Tanya Robbertze – a puppy raiser for South African Guide Dogs.
Tania:
Gladys was my lockdown dog. She crept into my heart. I absolutely adored that dog.
V/O ***
In 2022, shortly after Gladys became part of the Fani family, fate stepped in when Tania and a friend planned a visit to check in on Gladys and Busi.
Tania:
We hadn’t met Winston before and we were driving through Mfoleni which is a very confusing township and Google first of all can’t hold a signal inside of Umfoleni and second of all has got no idea of what roads are actual roads.
V/O **
Fortunately for Tania, Winston came to the rescue.
Winston said don’t worry I can give you directions. And he said describe to me what’s around you so I did and he said Oh travel down this road for probably another block, there is a green building there and it…
V/O **
Meticulously Winston guided Tania and her friend straight to his front door.
Tania: He wasn’t even in the car but his directions were spot on. It was mind blowing to be directed through a township with no markers that I could see by a blind man on the other end of the telephone.
UPS Winston:
If you look to your left hand side there is a beautiful view of Table Mountain
V/O *
Winston’s two-hour interactive walk starts in front of the Society for the Blind…
UPS Winston:
Those of you who are doing the tour with me for the first time can you please interact with me. Please let me know of unusual obstacles like a cars parked on the pavement don’t give me a hand just let me know
Masa: Let you know ok
V/O *
Born partially sighted, Winston was diagnosed with glaucoma, a progressive eye disease. He was around 13 years old when he lost his sight all together
Masa: Talk us through the extent of it what do you see?
Winston: I can differentiate when it's dark and when its light, and if I get closer to something like a pole or a tree I can see a shade ok but you start by sensing it because remember in the absence of my eyes all my other senses are strong to fill in that space, the missing space of my eyes.
UPS Winston:
What’s that thats drawn there?
It’s a screen of a cell phone…take a look
Masa I thought those were apartment blocks on top
V/O *
The insight Winston brings to the tour comes from detailed research, and conversations with the artists themselves.

Masa: Winston you just said Art is
Winston ‘ It’s a powerful tool of communication….it speaks in volumes
Masa: I love that.
V/O
But a tour guide is not a natural fit for a person without sight.
Winston: To be honest with you, I never thought of becoming a tourist guide at first up until I was retrenched from a company I was working for due to COVID…
V/O
Finding employment was a struggle. Busisiwe, Winston’s wife was the sole earner. They had to move to Mfuleni Township where Busi had family.
Masa: I am sorry to take you back to that time, but when you felt the walls were closing in, take us through that journey, for you and your wife Busisiwe.
Winston: She made me strong, because she took care of everything and it was not suiting me well, a soldier only dies once but a coward dies a thousand deaths. That’s what was frustrating me
Masa: On top of that you looking for a job and are visually impaired
Winston: That was a challenge I had to wrestle with that every day, you know men are born with ego. I tried to keep my cool but ya ego is there something a man is born with
[PAUSE]
V/O *
Winston & Busisiwe have been married for seven years.
Masa: Gladys you want to join us
Busisiwe: She is very special. And she makes me jealous because just like what you did you greet Gladys before you greet me Hey
LAUGHS
Masa: She is the star of the show
V/O *
Busisiwe lost her sight after a car accident in 2012.
Masa: What’s life like now?
Busi: It’s better than before, because I was very ignorant when I was sighted. If you’re a blind person, if you are doing something you have to use 200% rather than using 100%.
V/O
On the back of Winston’s impressive navigation skills Tania had a light bulb moment…
Tania: Winston would make a great tour guide because his attention to detail is amazing, his ability to communicate that to the people around him is absolutely incredible.
Winston: I saw an opportunity of being able to put food on the table again for my family being a provider I am not scared. I took it as a challenge.
Busisiswe
He is so work driven if he wants something he goes for it with a full potential and always positive about everything…
V/O *
The next step was fundraising for the tour guiding course. From Back-A-Buddy to Facebook… to reaching out to the media, Tania exploited all avenues.
Link
It was a radio interview that Winston was part of that was heard by just the right person that got the ball rolling
Enver : There was a plea from an operator talking about Winston’s story and his journey
V/O
Enver Duminy - CEO of Cape Town Tourism - saw an opportunity to make a difference.

Enver: I said what can we do as CT Tourism to make his dream come true of becoming a tourist guide.
Tania: And to his eternal credit Enver said yes whatever you need yes. Then we just had to find a tour guide company to train him.
Link
Being on Winston’s tours is truly remarkable he has such a deep understanding of the lay of the land. Understanding how many steps he needs to take to get to each pole to get to each street corner, bringing you from one beautiful art piece to the next. It’s a beautiful thing.
V/O *
Again …Tania played an integral part in Winston's preparation… She was his eyes, walking with him until he memorised the routes.
Winston: She gave me the landmarks and taught me how to navigate myself around this place. In order for you to be perfect in what you are doing you need to know how to create your own landmarks without having to see them. Only by bumping into something hard then you will know next time there is an obstacle there.
V/O
Winston took his first tour in July last year.
UPS Winston:
This is our local artist he’s from Jhb its showing us interaction between bees and human population and what would happen if there were no bees
Enver: Once you get to meet Winston and his ambition and what he wants to do, for us it was saying how can we change the status quo and CT is always portrayed as one of the most beautiful cities in the world but how do you see the city if you are blind, how do you experience it if you are blind and that became an eye opener for us … what can we do to get us to see our own city in a different light
Masa Here is the yellow Frame and the QR code is right here.
V/O
There are Braille Plaques and QR Codes – that link to recorded explanations by Winston - on the street art murals and the yellow frames dotted around the city’s Tourist Attractions - called Limitless Cape Town it’s a joint venture between Winston and Cape Town Tourism…
UPS Winston:
Winston: There are a few restaurants down Kremer Road, so I want to combine it do a three in one kind of a tour, street art, gin tasting and food tasting.
Masa Wow, we will come back for that.
V/O *
Winston has never been shy about taking on challenges… living his life not as a disabled person but what he calls a differently abled one. A characteristic Tania recognized when they first met
Tania: For the love of a dog we connected and for the love of a dog we could change the world for one person and who knows maybe they go on to change the world for someone else.
V/O
What started for Winston as a way of putting food on the table has developed into a passion to change the way he and other differently abled people live in the world, a world he believes has limitless possibilities.
